newsitem.title: USA: Hovnanian Q2 net contract could lag yr-ago.
newsitem.headline: Hovnanian Q2 net contract could lag yr-ago.

text.p: Hovnanian Enterprises Inc said Thursday its second quarter net contract performance could lag last year's record results, but it was confident revenues would meet or exceed last year's levels.

"Because last year's second quarter was an all time company record for any quarter, we would not be surprised if our fiscal 1997 second quarter net contract performance falls short of last year's results," Chairman Kevork Hovnanian said. "However, our net contract pace remains ahead of our expectations and we are confident that we will meet or exceed last year's revenue levels."
The company, which designs, constructs and markets single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums, reported a first quarter loss of $0.08 per share versus a profit of $0.02 per share.
Contract backlog rose to $335.0 million or 1,681 homes on January 31, 1997 compared with last year's $279.0 milion or 1,530 homes, the company said.

"Our first quarter is traditionally our weakest period," Hovnanian said. "Nonetheless, we feel that we remain on track to post fiscal year results similar to last year's $17.3 million of net income, with the third and fourth quarters once again being our most profitable quarters."
Hovnanian said most of the company's markets across the nation appeared to be firming, but consumers remained cautious and month-to-month sales results were difficult to forecast.
The more profitable active adult community homes were expected to represent about 15 percent of this year's deliveries, up from 1996's five percent, he said.
